Codegen type helpers

Source: R/codegen-ast.R
codegen-types.Rd

type_from_expr(e) deduces a codegen type from an expression, as SymPy's Type.from_expr. type_cast_check(t, value) casts value to type t and checks that the value did not change by more than the tolerance and that it lies in the type's range; type_cast_nocheck(t, value) casts without the checks. variable_deduced(symbol, value) builds a Variable() whose type is deduced from the symbol or the value, and as_Declaration(v, ...) turns a variable into a Declaration() with some fields replaced.

Usage

type_from_expr(e)

type_cast_nocheck(t, value)

type_cast_check(t, value, rtol = NULL, atol = 0)

variable_deduced(symbol, value = NULL, attrs = list(), cast_check = TRUE)

pointer_deduced(symbol, value = NULL, attrs = list(), cast_check = TRUE)

as_Declaration(v, ...)

from_FunctionDefinition(func_def)

from_FunctionPrototype(func_proto, body)

Arguments

e, value

An expression or number.

t

A codegen type such as real or float32.

rtol, atol

Relative and absolute tolerances.

symbol

A symbol.

attrs

Attributes of the variable.

cast_check

Check the cast of value.

v

A Variable().

...

Fields to replace.

func_def

A FunctionDefinition().

func_proto

A FunctionPrototype().

body

The body statements.

Value

A type, a number, or a node.

Examples

type_from_expr(Symbol("n", integer = TRUE))
#> integer
type_cast_check(int8, 127)
#> 127
variable_deduced(Symbol("x", real = TRUE))
#> Variable(x, type=real)
